     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field
    12	
    13	The identity component of the Picard scheme representing the **étale-sheafified**
    14	relative Picard functor — the Jacobian candidate of the headline, available for
    15	every smooth proper geometrically integral curve with **no hypothesis on
    16	`C(k)`** (owner decision of 2026-07-28, protection I-0491).
    17	
    18	## Why this file exists beside `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`
    19	
    20	That file develops `Pic⁰` for `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C = IdentityComponent
    21	(PicScheme C)`, the identity component of the scheme representing the
    22	*unsheafified* functor `picSharp C`. Since the owner decision, the sole producer
    23	of that scheme's existence gate is the conditional
    24	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so everything there is a statement about a
    25	**pointed** curve. Its mathematics is not wasted — the tangent-space chain and
    26	the dimension count are exactly the same arguments — but the *object* the
    27	headline needs is the identity component of `PicSchemeEt C`.
    28	
    29	Two of the four abelian-variety properties come for free at this level, and two
    30	do not, which is the same split as in the `picSharp` development:
    31	
    32	* `Pic0Et.grpObj` and `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible` are **proved** here, from
    33	  the unconditional `groupSchemeStructureEt` and
    34	  `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`;
    35	* `Pic0Et.isSeparated` is **proved**, from the unconditional separatedness of
    36	  `PicSchemeEt` along the clopen immersion;
    37	* `Pic0Et.smooth` and `Pic0Et.proper` are the two remaining obligations of the
    38	  headline, and both are stated here as **assemblies** rather than as bare
    39	  `sorry`s, following the run-0067 reduction of the `picSharp` side
    40	  (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`). Their actual residues are one statement
    41	  each:
    42	  - `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` — Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero, a
    43	    genuine statement in characteristic `p`. Everything else in smoothness is
    44	    mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` plus the two inputs proved above;
    45	  - `Pic0Et.universallyClosed` — Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`. The other two
    46	    conjuncts of properness (separatedness, local finiteness) are proved.
    47	
    48	  Both residues are **true statements**, in contrast with the deleted
    49	  rational-point leaf, which was false.
    50	
    51	## References
    52	
    53	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §5 (`lem:agps`, `prp:pic0`,
    54	Thm. `thm:tgtsp`). Blueprint: `def:pic_zero_subscheme`,
    55	`thm:pic_zero_is_abelian_variety`.
    56	-/

    60	universe u
    61	
    62	open CategoryTheory
    63	
    64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    65	
    66	namespace Scheme
    67	
    68	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field**: the identity component of the
    69	scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
    70	
    71	Unconditional — no `[HasRationalPoint C]`, and no `[HasPicScheme C]`. The two
    72	inputs `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` requires are both available for
    73	`PicSchemeEt C` without hypotheses on `C(k)`: the group structure
    74	`groupSchemeStructureEt` (Yoneda transport of the étale sheaf's abelian-group
    75	structure) and `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1),
    76	extracted from the representability package).
    77	
    78	This is the Jacobian candidate of the headline. When `genus C = 0` it is
    79	`Spec k`, with no separate construction: the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is then
    80	`0`-dimensional. -/

    82	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    83	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    84	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    85	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    86	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicSchemeEt C)
    87	
    88	namespace Pic0Et

    90	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is a group scheme** — PROVED, unconditionally.
    91	
    92	The identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type is an open
    93	and closed subgroup scheme (`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`,
    94	Kleiman §5 Lem. `lem:agps`(3)), and its group structure is the one transported
    95	onto `PicSchemeEt C` from the étale Picard sheaf by
    96	`groupSchemeStructureEt`. Neither step needs a rational point.

    99	substrate delivers the subgroup-scheme structure existentially. -/

   102	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

   108	
   109	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` (Kleiman §5
   110	Lem. `lem:agps`): the identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite
   111	type is locally of finite type, quasi-compact and geometrically irreducible. Only
   112	the third conjunct is taken here. -/
   113	theorem geometricallyIrreducible {k : Type u} [Field k]
   114	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   115	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   116	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   117	    GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   118	  (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
   119	    (PicSchemeEt C)).2.2
   120	
   121	/-- `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is locally of finite type over `k` — PROVED, unconditionally
   122	(first conjunct of `isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`). -/
   123	theorem locallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
   124	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   125	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   126	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   127	    LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   128	  (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
   129	    (PicSchemeEt C)).1

   131	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
   132	statement.
   133	
   134	Kleiman §5: a group scheme locally of finite type over a field is smooth as soon
   135	as it is geometrically reduced. Mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` takes exactly
   136	`[LocallyOfFiniteType f]`, `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` and `[GeometricallyReduced f]`
   137	over an arbitrary field, and the first two are proved above
   138	(`locallyOfFiniteType`, `grpObj`). So the entire remaining content is
   139	`GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom` — Cartier's theorem in
   140	characteristic zero, and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise. It
   141	does not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is

    13	
    14	The two remaining obligations of `Picard/Pic0Et.lean` —
    15	`Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` (`:170`) and
    16	`Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed` (`:223`) — are among the **five** obligations
    17	named under `picardJacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`), which is the headline's
    18	witness. This file reduces each of them to a statement about a **single scheme**,
    19	and proves that both reductions are *equivalences* rather than weakenings.
    20	
    21	**The five obligations are not independent, and the list reads as if they were.**
    22	`Jacobian.lean`'s enumeration and this file's first draft both invited the reader to
    23	count `geometricallyReduced` and `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` (obligation
    24	4, `Jacobian.lean:454`) as two separate distances. They are not: obligation 4 implies
    25	this file's reducedness target, since
    26	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced (genus C)` yields
    27	`GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom` directly. Measured here and independently
    28	by the lane holding obligation 4 (inbox `I-1040`, `I-1039`). The arrow runs 4 ⟹ 2, so
    29	nothing proved about the reducedness half is wasted — but a reader adding the two gets
    30	a remaining distance that is too long by one.
    31	
    32	The **properness** half below is genuinely independent of obligation 4, and
    33	`quasiCompact` is the reason it is reachable at all on this tower.
    34	
    35	## What is proved here, and what is not
    36	
    37	**Proved.** Four reductions and their four converses, all sorry-free:
    38	
    39	* `geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` — reducedness of
    40	  the one scheme `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` gives `GeometricallyReduced` of the
    41	  structure morphism, hence (`smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`)
    42	  smoothness. No quantifier over field extensions.
    43	* `isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange_of_geometricallyReduced` — the converse,
    44	  so the hypothesis above is **equivalent** to the obligation, packaged as
    45	  `geometricallyReduced_iff_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`.
    46	* `universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion` / `proper_of_valuativeCriterion` — the
    47	  valuative route to properness, whose `QuasiCompact` side condition is *free* on
    48	  this tower (`quasiCompact` below).
    49	* `universallyClosed_of_baseChange` and its converse
    50	  `universallyClosed_iff_baseChange` — universal closedness is fpqc-local, so it
    51	  too reduces to `k̄` losslessly.
    52	
    53	**Not proved, and not weakened.** `IsReduced (Pic⁰ ×_k k̄)` and
    54	`ValuativeCriterion.Existence` are **hypotheses** in every statement below. This
    55	file does not witness either one for any curve; it shows that each obligation *is*
    56	one single-scheme statement and nothing else. The two `sorry`s in `Pic0Et.lean`
    57	stay exactly where they are — see "Honest accounting" below.
    58	
    59	## Why this was worth doing: the picSharp side had it and the étale side did not
    60	
    61	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` carries all four of these reductions for
    62	`Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, the identity component of the scheme representing the
    63	*unsheafified* functor. Every one of them binds `[HasPicScheme C]`, a class with
    64	**no instance** — its only producer is the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
    65	and `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` was deleted as false (protection `I-0491`). So the
    66	picSharp reductions, correct as they are, are statements about no curve.
    67	
    68	The headline's object is `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C`. Its gate `[HasPicSchemeEt C]` is
    69	unconditionally inhabited. Transporting the reductions therefore moves them from a
    70	tower nothing inhabits onto the tower `picardJacobianWitness` actually uses.
    71	
    72	**The transport is not automatic and half of it was recorded as unmeasured.** The
    73	smoothness half was measured to transfer in a scratch file by a review pass (inbox
    74	`I-0944`) and is landed here. The properness half was explicitly *not*:
    75	`AJC.pic0av.structure` said "`universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion` is stated for

    77	carries to `Pic0SchemeEt` is unmeasured, so do not assume it". It does carry, and

    79	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` is available for

    81	
    82	## Two measured negatives, recorded so they are not retried
    83	
    84	* **`IsProper` does not fpqc-descend at this mathlib.** Only its `UniversallyClosed`

    87	  `descendsAlong_universallyClosed_surjective_inf_flat_inf_quasicompact` is an
    88	  instance. So properness must be assembled conjunct-by-conjunct after descending
    89	  the closedness half — which is what `proper_of_baseChange` does.
    90	* **Mathlib has no Cartier theorem.** There is no result in
    91	  `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry` making a group scheme reduced in characteristic zero,
    92	  and no `CharZero` hypothesis anywhere in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/`. The
    93	  reducedness input below is therefore genuine mathematics and not a missing
    94	  `import`; a lane looking for a cheap discharge of it will not find one in the
    95	  pinned mathlib.
    96	* **There is no perfect-field shortcut, and this is the tempting wrong turn.**
    97	  Mathlib's generic smoothness `Scheme.Hom.dense_smoothLocus_of_perfectField` takes
    98	  `[PerfectField K] [IsReduced X]` — no algebraic closure — which suggests replacing

   102	  `pointEquivClosedPoint`, and elaborating it under `[PerfectField k]` alone fails to
   103	  synthesize `IsAlgClosed k`. Generic smoothness is only one of the two inputs; the
   104	  transitivity of translations on closed points is the other, and that one really does
   105	  want an algebraically closed field. So the `k̄` base change is not a convenience of
   106	  the statement — it is where the argument lives.
   107	
   108	  Note the ring-level shape confirms this is the standard formulation:
   109	  `Algebra.isGeometricallyReduced_iff` *defines* geometric reducedness as
   110	  `IsReduced (k̄ ⊗[k] A)`. The equivalence proved below is the scheme-level image of
   111	  that iff, not a project-specific weakening.

   113	## Honest accounting
   114	
   115	**The hypotheses are not free — measured, and one of the four checks does not apply.**
   116	Three of the four antecedents used below fail to synthesize on their own, so the
   117	reductions are not vacuous: `IsReduced (Pic⁰ ×_k k̄)`, `UniversallyClosed` of the `k̄`

   121	definition, so no `infer_instance` test is meaningful for it and no such test is
   122	claimed here. Its non-freeness rests on the ordinary observation that it is an
   123	explicit hypothesis of the two theorems that use it and is discharged nowhere in this
   124	project.
   125	
   126	Every declaration in this file binds `[Scheme.HasPicSchemeEt C]`. That class *does*
   127	have an unconditional instance, but that instance is
   128	`(Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability C).1` — a projection of the project's central
   129	`sorry`. So the theorems here are axiom-clean **as implications** and
   130	`sorry`-reachable **on instantiation** at any curve (the shape recorded in inbox

   162	`Pic⁰_{C/k}`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, a **true** statement.
   163	
   164	Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero; in characteristic `p` a genuine
   165	statement (it is where `H²(C, 𝒪_C) = 0` enters on the `picSharp` side). It does
   166	not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is
   167	`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular here.
   168	
   169	This is the étale counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyReduced`. -/
   170	theorem geometricallyReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
   171	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   172	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   173	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   174	    GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   175	  sorry
   176	
   177	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — assembly of
   178	`smooth_of_geometricallyReduced` with its single open input. -/
   179	theorem smooth {k : Type u} [Field k]
   180	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   181	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   182	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   183	    Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   184	  smooth_of_geometricallyReduced C (geometricallyReduced C)
   185	
   186	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
   187	statement.
   188	
   189	Kleiman §5 Prp. `prp:pic0`: the identity component of the Picard scheme of a
   190	smooth proper curve is proper (indeed projective) over the base. Quasi-compactness
   191	of the identity component is available
   192	(`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`, second
   193	conjunct) and separatedness descends from `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated` along the
   194	clopen immersion; what is missing is universal closedness, which is where the
   195	properness of `C` enters through the Abel map.
   196	
   197	This is the étale-formulation counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.proper`, and it is one
   198	of the five obligations of the Jacobian headline. As with smoothness, it is stated
   199	as an **assembly**: two of the three conjuncts of properness are proved, so the
   200	obligation proper is `universallyClosed` below. -/
   201	theorem isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k]
   202	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   203	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   204	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   205	    IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   206	  obtain ⟨⟨f, hopen, -⟩⟩ :=
   207	    GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme (PicSchemeEt C)
   208	  haveI := hopen
   209	  change IsSeparated (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicSchemeEt C)).hom
   210	  rw [← Over.w f]
   211	  infer_instance
   212	
   213	/-- **The sole remaining input to properness: universal closedness of
   214	`Pic⁰_{C/k}`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, a **true** statement.
   215	
   216	Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`: a smooth proper curve is geometrically normal, so the
   217	projectivity upgrade applies to its Picard scheme and the identity component is
   218	proper. Separatedness (`isSeparated` above, from `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`
   219	along the clopen immersion) and local finiteness (`locallyOfFiniteType`) are the
   220	two conjuncts that are proved; this is the third.
   221	
   222	This is the étale counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.universallyClosed`. -/
   223	theorem universallyClosed {k : Type u} [Field k]
   224	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   225	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   226	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   227	    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   228	  sorry
   229	
   230	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k`** — assembly of the two proved conjuncts
   231	with the single open one. -/
   232	theorem proper {k : Type u} [Field k]
   233	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   234	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   235	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   236	    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   237	  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
   238	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
   239	  haveI := universallyClosed C

     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Integral
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Smooth
     8	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.FractionRing
     9	import Mathlib.RingTheory.RingHom.StandardSmooth
    10	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Smooth.Flat
    11	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Unramified.Field
    12	
    13	/-!
    14	# Smooth morphisms are geometrically reduced
    15	
    16	A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum of a
    17	field is reduced. Combined with geometric irreducibility, this upgrades the standing hypotheses
    18	of the Jacobian challenge (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom` and
    19	`GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom`) to `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`, which is what all the
    20	actual geometry of the project consumes.
    21	
    22	The commutative-algebra core is that a standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. By the
    23	structure theorem for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7,
    24	`RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.exists_etale_mvPolynomial`), such an algebra `S` is étale over a
    25	polynomial ring `P` over the base. Since `S` is flat over the domain `P`, it embeds into
    26	`Frac(P) ⊗[P] S`, which is formally unramified and essentially of finite type over the field
    27	`Frac(P)`, hence reduced by `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field`.
    28	
    29	## Main results
    30	
    31	* `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain`: a flat, formally unramified algebra,
    32	  essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    33	* `Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain`, `RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`,
    34	  `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`: étale/standard smooth algebras over
    35	  domains are reduced.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.isReduced_of_field`: a scheme smooth over `Spec` of a field is
    37	  reduced.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced`: a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced
    39	  (instance), together with the `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyIntegral`: a smooth, geometrically irreducible
    41	  morphism is geometrically integral (instance), together with the
    42	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    43	
    44	This file is written in mathlib generality and is a candidate for upstreaming. It was
    45	developed in the sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`
    46	(`AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`) and imported here unchanged; it
    47	depends on Mathlib only, so the two copies can be kept in step by file copy until one
    48	of them is upstreamed.
    49	
    50	In this project it closes the geometric-integrality half of the headline's hypothesis
    51	gap: `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` are stated for a
    52	smooth proper **geometrically irreducible** curve, while the Picard/FGA development
    53	runs under `GeometricallyIntegral`. `Smooth.geometricallyIntegral` bridges the two, so
    54	the only remaining hypothesis gap at the headline is the `k`-rational point, which is a
    55	genuine mathematical gap rather than missing infrastructure (see
    56	`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`, leaf `hasRationalPoint_of_curve`).
    57	-/
    58	
    59	set_option autoImplicit false
    60	
    61	universe u
    62	
    63	open TensorProduct
    64	
    65	section RingTheory
    66	
    67	/-- A flat, formally unramified algebra, essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    68	This generalizes `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field` from fields to domains, at the
    69	price of the flatness assumption (which is automatic over a field). -/
    70	theorem Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    71	    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified B S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType B S]
    72	    [Module.Flat B S] : IsReduced S := by
    73	  have : IsReduced (FractionRing B ⊗[B] S) :=
    74	    Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field (FractionRing B) (FractionRing B ⊗[B] S)
    75	  refine isReduced_of_injective
    76	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := B) (A := FractionRing B) (B := S)) ?_
    77	  have h : ⇑(Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := B) (A := FractionRing B) (B := S)) =
    78	      ⇑(LinearMap.rTensor S (Algebra.ofId B (FractionRing B)).toLinearMap) ∘
    79	        ⇑(TensorProduct.lid B S).symm := by
    80	    ext s
    81	    simp
    82	  rw [h]
    83	  exact (Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
    84	    (IsFractionRing.injective B (FractionRing B))).comp (TensorProduct.lid B S).symm.injective
    85	
    86	/-- An étale algebra over a domain is reduced. -/
    87	theorem Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S] [IsDomain B]
    88	    [Algebra B S] [Algebra.Etale B S] : IsReduced S :=
    89	  Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain B S
    90	
    91	/-- The target of a standard smooth ring homomorphism out of a domain is reduced: by
    92	Stacks 00T7 it is étale over a polynomial ring over the base, and étale algebras over
    93	domains are reduced. -/
    94	theorem RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain {B S : Type*} [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    95	    [IsDomain B] {g : B →+* S} (hg : g.IsStandardSmooth) : IsReduced S := by
    96	  obtain ⟨n, φ, -, hφ⟩ := hg.exists_etale_mvPolynomial
    97	  algebraize [φ]
    98	  exact Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain (MvPolynomial (Fin n) B) S
    99	
   100	/-- A standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. -/
   101	theorem Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
   102	    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.IsStandardSmooth B S] : IsReduced S :=
   103	  (RingHom.isStandardSmooth_algebraMap.mpr ‹_›).isReduced_of_isDomain
   104	
   105	end RingTheory
   106	
   107	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   108	
   109	open CategoryTheory Limits
   110	
   111	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
   112	
   113	/-- A scheme smooth over the spectrum of a field is reduced. -/
   114	theorem Smooth.isReduced_of_field {K : Type u} [Field K] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [Smooth f] :
   115	    IsReduced X := by
   116	  have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   117	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
   118	  choose U hU V hV hxV e hsm using Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth f
   119	  -- Each chart is the spectrum of a standard smooth algebra over (a ring isomorphic to) `K`,
   120	  -- hence reduced.
   121	  have hred (x : X) : IsReduced (V x).toScheme := by
   122	    have : IsAffine (V x).toScheme := hV x
   123	    have hfx : f x ∈ U x := e x (hxV x)
   124	    have hUx : U x = ⊤ := by
   125	      refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y ↦ ?_)
   126	      exact Subsingleton.elim (f x) y ▸ hfx
   127	    have hdom : IsDomain Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), U x) := by
   128	      rw [hUx]
   129	      exact Function.Injective.isDomain
   130	        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv (RingEquiv.injective _)
   131	    have hΓ : _root_.IsReduced Γ(X, V x) := (hsm x).isReduced_of_isDomain
   132	    have : _root_.IsReduced Γ((V x).toScheme, ⊤) :=
   133	      isReduced_of_injective (V x).topIso.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv (RingEquiv.injective _)
   134	    exact isReduced_of_isAffine_isReduced _
   135	  let 𝒰 : X.OpenCover := Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers X (fun x ↦ (V x).toScheme) (fun x ↦ (V x).ι)
   136	    (fun x ↦ ⟨x, ⟨x, hxV x⟩, rfl⟩) (fun x ↦ inferInstance)
   137	  have : ∀ i, IsReduced (𝒰.X i) := hred
   138	  exact IsReduced.of_openCover _ 𝒰
   139	
   140	/-- A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum
   141	of a field is smooth over that field, hence reduced. -/
   142	instance (priority := 100) Smooth.geometricallyReduced (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f] :
   143	    GeometricallyReduced f where
   144	  geometrically_isReduced := fun K _ y Z fst snd h ↦
   145	    have : Smooth snd := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Smooth) h ‹Smooth f›
   146	    Smooth.isReduced_of_field snd
   147	
   148	/-- A morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth. This is the relative dimension of
   149	the curve bundle of the Jacobian challenge; the general statement is
   150	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth`, which cannot be an instance since `n` does not occur in
   151	the conclusion. -/
   152	instance (priority := 100) Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one (f : X ⟶ Y)
   153	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] : Smooth f :=
   154	  SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth 1 f
   155	
   156	/-- A morphism smooth of some relative dimension is geometrically reduced. Not an instance
   157	since `n` cannot be inferred from the conclusion; for relative dimension `1`, instance
   158	resolution goes through `Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`. -/
   159	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced (n : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
   160	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] : GeometricallyReduced f :=
   161	  have : Smooth f := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth n f
   162	  inferInstance
   163	
   164	/-- A smooth, geometrically irreducible morphism is geometrically integral. -/
   165	instance (priority := 100) Smooth.geometricallyIntegral (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f]
   166	    [GeometricallyIrreducible f] : GeometricallyIntegral f :=
   167	  .of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible f
   168	
   169	/-- A geometrically irreducible morphism, smooth of some relative dimension, is geometrically
   170	integral. Not an instance since `n` cannot be inferred from the conclusion. -/
   171	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyIntegral (n : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
   172	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] [GeometricallyIrreducible f] : GeometricallyIntegral f :=
   173	  have : Smooth f := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth n f
   174	  .of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible f
   175	
   176	section CurveBundle
   177	
   178	/-! Instance-resolution smoke tests for the hypothesis bundle of the Jacobian challenge
   179	(the `IsProper` hypothesis is omitted as it plays no role here): the curve `C` is
   180	geometrically reduced and geometrically integral, by `inferInstance`. -/
   181	
   182	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   183	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   184	
   185	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
   186	example : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom := inferInstance
   187	
   188	end CurveBundle
   189	
   190	end AlgebraicGeometry

    13	/-!
    14	# Smooth morphisms are geometrically reduced
    15	
    16	A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum of a
    17	field is reduced. Combined with geometric irreducibility, this upgrades the standing hypotheses
    18	of the Jacobian challenge (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom` and
    19	`GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom`) to `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`, which is what all the
    20	actual geometry of the project consumes.
    21	
    22	The commutative-algebra core is that a standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. By the
    23	structure theorem for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7,
    24	`RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.exists_etale_mvPolynomial`), such an algebra `S` is étale over a
    25	polynomial ring `P` over the base. Since `S` is flat over the domain `P`, it embeds into
    26	`Frac(P) ⊗[P] S`, which is formally unramified and essentially of finite type over the field
    27	`Frac(P)`, hence reduced by `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field`.
    28	
    29	## Main results
    30	
    31	* `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain`: a flat, formally unramified algebra,
    32	  essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
    33	* `Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain`, `RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`,
    34	  `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain`: étale/standard smooth algebras over
    35	  domains are reduced.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.isReduced_of_field`: a scheme smooth over `Spec` of a field is
    37	  reduced.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced`: a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced
    39	  (instance), together with the `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyIntegral`: a smooth, geometrically irreducible
    41	  morphism is geometrically integral (instance), together with the
    42	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` variant.
    43	
    44	This file is written in mathlib generality and is a candidate for upstreaming. It was
    45	developed in the sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`
    46	(`AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`) and imported here unchanged; it
    47	depends on Mathlib only, so the two copies can be kept in step by file copy until one
    48	of them is upstreamed.

    50	In this project it closes the geometric-integrality half of the headline's hypothesis

/-! ### The étale leaves: B and C for the headline witness

The two leaves above and below are stated for `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, the identity
component of the scheme representing the *unsheafified* functor, so they carry
`[Scheme.HasPicScheme C]` — a hypothesis whose only producer is now the conditional
`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. The headline witness is assembled instead from
`Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C` (`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`), so it needs the same two statements
there. These are those statements. Each is a **true** statement awaiting a proof, and
neither carries a hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/

/-- **Leaf B, étale formulation: the dimension refinement.**

`Scheme.Pic0Et.smooth` gives bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over `k`; the witness field
`smoothGenus` needs it at the specific relative dimension `genus C`. Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11:
the tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, of dimension `genus C` by definition
of `genus`, and for a smooth group scheme the relative dimension is the dimension of that
tangent space.

What it owes over and above the `picSharp` leaf `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` is
the same two steps recorded there — `Pic0Et.smooth` itself, plus the translation between
a tangent-space dimension and Mathlib's presentation-based `SmoothOfRelativeDimension`
(which is characterised by `Module.rank S Ω[S⁄R]`, a different invariant).

**And nothing more — corrected 2026-07-29 (`ajc-p2`), because the previous text priced
this leaf on a transport that is not needed.** That text said the dimension chain
`Scheme.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` "is stated for `Pic0Scheme`,
so transporting it to `Pic0SchemeEt` needs the comparison of the two Picard schemes,
which is available only under a section", and called that "the honest remaining cost".
Two defects, both measured:

* the chain does not need transporting, because it **restates** at `Pic0SchemeEt` with no
  comparison anywhere. Every engine of its dual-number leg is quantified over an arbitrary
  functor and an arbitrary `RepresentableBy`
  (`Pic0.pointedDualNumberPointsEquivAddKernel`,
  `pointedDualNumberPointsEquivOfOpenImmersion`,
  `overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual`,
  `nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq`); `picSharp` entered only at the
  *application* sites. Applying them at `(PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj` with
  `representableEt` gives the whole chain unconditionally, in
  `Picard/Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean` — including the representability leg against `picEt`
  (`Pic0Et.pointedDualNumberPoints_equiv_relPicEtKernel`, axiom-clean) and the keystone
  `Pic0Et.tangentSpaceIso`. Since a section is exactly what protection `I-0491` forbids
  the headline to carry, the old pricing put this leaf behind a specification change it
  does not in fact need;
* "the **landed** dimension chain" was wrong on its own terms:
  `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` reports `sorryAx`, through
  `Pic0.semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`. This file already says so 50
  lines below, at `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus`.

What the étale dimension count actually costs is **one** statement, and it is the same one
the pointed development owes: `Pic0Et.SemilinearCotangentComparisonEt`, the étale
restatement of that `sorry`. `Pic0Et.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_genus` is proved from it,
so leaf B's dimension number is not the open part — the two `SmoothOfRelativeDimension`
translation steps above are, and they are shared with the pointed leaf. -/

    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=

/-- **Leaf B's dimension count, at the headline and against the `picSharp` development.**

The number `genus C` in leaf B is not an arbitrary index: it is the dimension of the
Zariski tangent space of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` at the identity
(`Scheme.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne`, the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11
chain through the truncated-exponential splitting and the Mayer–Vietoris comparison).
Since `genus C` is by definition `dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, the two sides match with no
transport, exactly as leaf C's `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` matches
`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property`.

That chain is **not landed** — an earlier version of this docstring called it "landed
mathematics", contradicting what this very declaration records below, that its axioms
carry `sorryAx`. Both legs of it are proved; the residue is one statement,
`Pic0.semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`. Corrected 2026-07-29 (`ajc-p2`).

Stating it here fixes what leaf B still owes, which is easy to misjudge from the leaf
alone. It is *not* the dimension count. It is the two steps that turn a tangent-space
dimension into a relative dimension:

1. `Scheme.Pic0.smooth` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over `k`, itself `sorry`-bodied
   upstream, so leaf B presupposes an obligation rather than reducing one. That obligation
   is smaller than it looks, and worth stating here because it changes what a reader should
   expect to have to build: its *entire* remaining content is
   `GeometricallyReduced (Pic⁰_{C/k}).hom`. Mathlib's public `smooth_of_grpObj` takes
   `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]`, `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` and `[GeometricallyReduced f]` and
   returns `Smooth f` over an arbitrary field, so the translation argument that propagates
   smoothness from the identity is already done there; the first two inputs are landed
   (`Pic0.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0.grpObj`) and elaborate at these hypotheses verbatim,
   while `GeometricallyReduced` does not synthesize and its only producer in the tree is
   `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular. So `Pic0.smooth` is Cartier's
   theorem in characteristic zero and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise —
   not a translation argument. "Entire remaining content" is meant strictly, and it is
   measured rather than estimated: the conclusion of `Pic0.smooth`, proved at that
   theorem's binders verbatim with `GeometricallyReduced` as the sole added hypothesis, is
   **axiom-clean** — `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, where `Pic0.smooth` itself
   reports `sorryAx`. So supplying geometric reducedness discharges it outright, with no
   residual leak elsewhere in the assembly;
2. the passage from "smooth, with `dim_{κ(e)} T_e = n`" to
   `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n`. Mathlib defines the latter by local standard-smooth
   presentations, not by a tangent-space dimension. There *is* a bridge, but it is at the
   algebra level and it goes through a different invariant:
   `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth` characterises
   relative dimension `n` as `Module.rank S Ω[S⁄R] = n`, the rank of the module of Kähler
   differentials. So the missing mathematics is (i) the identification of that rank with
   the tangent-space dimension at the identity — over a field these are dual to one
   another, but the statement has to be made and the duality is where a rank/`finrank`
   mismatch would bite — and (ii) the passage from an affine-local statement about
   presentations to the scheme-level class, which quantifies over an affine cover of
   `Pic⁰_{C/k}` rather than over a single point.

   This is worth stating precisely rather than as "no bridge exists", which an earlier
   version of this docstring claimed: the leaf's cost is a translation between two
   invariants of smoothness, not the construction of one from nothing.

Like `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`, this is a faithful record of a distance rather
than a discharge: its axioms carry `sorryAx`, because the dimension chain it invokes
still rests on `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_finrank_h1Cok`. -/

    95	locally-of-finite-type-plus-quasi-compact (i.e., of finite type) over `k`,
    96	and is geometrically irreducible. The proof reduces (after base change to
    97	`\bar k`) to picking a nonempty irreducible open subset `U ⊆ G^0`; the
    98	translates `zg⁻¹U` give an open cover of the closed points of `G^0` by
    99	irreducible neighbourhoods, extended to all points by Jacobson density, so
   100	with connectedness this gives irreducibility globally (EGA I 6.1.10). The
   101	image `α(W × W) ⊆ G^0` of an affine open `W ∋ e` under the group law is
   102	quasi-compact and contains all closed points, so finitely many affine opens
   103	cover `G^0` and `G^0` is quasi-compact.
   104	
   105	The three conjuncts are obtained as follows: `LocallyOfFiniteType` because
   106	the structural morphism is an open immersion composed with `G.hom`;
   107	`QuasiCompact` from `identityComponent_compactSpace` (Kleiman's product trick
   108	over the algebraic closure, Jacobson density, and descent along the
   109	surjective base-change projection) together with the affine-target
   110	characterisation of quasi-compactness; `GeometricallyIrreducible` from
   111	`identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible` (translation of an irreducible
   112	open through all closed points over the algebraic closure, EGA I 6.1.10, and
   113	descent along the surjective projection from the algebraic closure of each
   114	field extension). -/
   115	theorem IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
   116	    {k : Type u} [Field k]
   117	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   118	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   119	    LocallyOfFiniteType (IdentityComponent G).hom ∧
   120	      QuasiCompact (IdentityComponent G).hom ∧
   121	      GeometricallyIrreducible (IdentityComponent G).hom := by
   122	  refine ⟨identityComponent_locallyOfFiniteType G, ?_,
   123	    identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible G⟩
   124	  haveI h : CompactSpace (IdentityComponent G).left := identityComponent_compactSpace G
   125	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr h
   126	
   127	end GroupScheme

   133	integral curve `C/k` (from sibling `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).

   144	`Pic_{C/k}` (from sibling `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`,

   147	open and closed subgroup scheme of `Pic_{C/k}` of finite type over `k`,

     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Smooth
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Smoothness of a group scheme from reducedness over ONE algebraic closure
    10	
    11	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj` proves that a group scheme locally of finite
    12	type over a field is smooth as soon as it is **geometrically** reduced, i.e. as soon as
    13	`X ×_k Spec K` is reduced for *every* field `K` and every `Spec K ⟶ Spec k`. Internally it
    14	goes through a `private` lemma which needs only reducedness of the **single** base change to
    15	the algebraic closure — the geometric content is the translation argument at an algebraically
    16	closed base, and the general field case is obtained by flat descent along `Spec k̄ → Spec k`.
    17	
    18	That `private` modifier is the whole reason for this file. Both this project and the sibling
    19	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` reached the same conclusion independently (inbox
    20	I-0495, 2026-07-28): the smoothness leg of "`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety" wants to
    21	supply reducedness over `k̄` and nothing more, because
    22	
    23	* `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced` is *defined* by base change to an algebraic closure
    24	  (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Nilpotent/GeometricallyReduced.lean`), so at the algebra level the
    25	  k̄-statement is the definition rather than a special case;
    26	* the scheme-level class `GeometricallyReduced` quantifies over all field base changes, and
    27	  the passage from the `k̄` case to that quantifier is **absent from mathlib v4.31** — it is
    28	  the transcendental half of `IsReduced after base change to k̄ ⟹ GeometricallyReduced`,
    29	  which has no producer in mathlib and no `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong` instance either
    30	  (verified by machine on both sides, recorded on inbox I-0495).
    31	
    32	So the honest input to smoothness is the `k̄` one, and the cross-project thread priced getting
    33	it as *an upstream PR making `smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` public*. It is cheaper than
    34	that: the `private` proof uses only public API, so it can simply be re-derived here. This
    35	file does that and then packages the descent step, giving a smoothness criterion whose
    36	hypothesis is a single `IsReduced`.
    37	
    38	## Main results
    39	
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed'` — the re-derivation of mathlib's
    41	  `private` lemma: a reduced group scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed
    42	  field is smooth. Proof transcribed from `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`
    43	  (Andrew Yang), which is why the `set_option`s and the `open`s are the same.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` — the
    45	  criterion this project actually consumes: `G ⟶ Spec k` is smooth as soon as the base change
    46	  `G ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` is reduced. No `GeometricallyReduced`, no quantifier over fields.
    47	
    48	## Change of attack surface, NOT of strength — corrected after review
    49	
    50	An earlier version of this docstring called the criterion's hypothesis **strictly weaker** than
    51	`smooth_of_grpObj`'s. **That is wrong in this project, and the correction is the interesting
    52	part.** Fresh-context review (run 0067) established:
    53	
    54	* in **mathlib alone**, `IsReduced`-over-`k̄ ⟹ GeometricallyReduced` is indeed unavailable —
    55	  `infer_instance` fails for it on a bare `import Mathlib`;
    56	* but **this project owns the converse**: `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`
    57	  (`AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`, an instance) derives the class from
    58	  smoothness. So `IsReduced`-over-`k̄` → (this criterion) → `Smooth` → `GeometricallyReduced`
    59	  closes by `inferInstance`, axiom-clean.
    60	
    61	At these binders the two hypotheses are therefore **interprovable**, and this file is a
    62	restatement rather than a weakening. The mistake was methodological and worth recording: the
    63	"missing in mathlib" measurement was taken inside the *edited file's* import cone (99 modules),
    64	which does not contain `Curve/GeometricallyReduced`, while the root cone (215 modules) does.
    65	A synthesis probe cannot see a bridge its own imports exclude — measure at the root.
    66	
    67	**What the restatement is still good for**, which is why it stays: the two hypotheses are
    68	equivalent but not equally *attackable*. `GeometricallyReduced` quantifies over every field
    69	extension and has no producer here other than the circular one; reducedness of one scheme over
    70	one algebraically closed field is where Kleiman §5's argument (and Cartier's theorem in
    71	characteristic zero) actually speaks. Same strength, better attack surface.
    72	
    73	**And the corollary the first version missed**: since the criterion yields `Smooth` and
    74	`Smooth.geometricallyReduced` yields the class, the `k̄` hypothesis discharges
    75	`Pic0.geometricallyReduced` — an open `sorry` of `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` — as well as
    76	the smoothness leg. One statement, two obligations. Verified axiom-clean at the root; see
    77	`Pic0.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` there.
    78	
    79	## References
    80	
    81	Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`; Kleiman, "The Picard scheme"
    82	(arXiv:math/0504020), §5. Cross-project analysis: inbox I-0495 (2026-07-28).
    83	-/

    86	
    87	universe u
    88	
    89	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
    90	
    91	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    92	
    93	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {G : Scheme.{u}} (f : G ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    94	    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [GrpObj (Over.mk f)]
    95	
    96	set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
    97	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    98	open MonObj MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory in
    99	/-- **A reduced group scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field is
   100	smooth** — the re-derivation of mathlib's `private smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed`.
   101	
   102	The mathematics is not ours: the proof below is transcribed from
   103	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean` (Andrew Yang), which is why the `set_option`s,
   104	the `open`s and the tactic script agree with it line for line. It is re-derived rather than
   105	imported because the mathlib declaration is `private`, and its statement — reducedness over
   106	*one* algebraically closed field — is the hypothesis this project can actually supply, while
   107	the public `smooth_of_grpObj` asks for the full `GeometricallyReduced` class.
   108	
   109	The argument itself: the smooth locus is nonempty (generic smoothness over a perfect field)
   110	and stable under the translation isomorphisms `GrpObj.mulRight`, which act transitively on
   111	closed points; a Jacobson space whose points are closed-point-dense then forces the smooth
   112	locus to be everything. -/
   113	theorem smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed' [IsReduced G] [IsAlgClosed K] : Smooth f := by
   114	  have := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace f
   115	  have : Nonempty G := ⟨η[Over.mk f].1 (IsLocalRing.closedPoint _)⟩
   116	  rw [← Scheme.Hom.smoothLocus_eq_top_iff, ← TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_eq_univ,
   117	    ← not_ne_iff, ← Set.nonempty_compl]
   118	  intro H
   119	  obtain ⟨x, hx, hxc⟩ :=
   120	    nonempty_inter_closedPoints H f.smoothLocus.2.isClosed_compl.isLocallyClosed
   121	  obtain ⟨y, hy : y ∈ f.smoothLocus, hyc⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints
   122	    f.dense_smoothLocus_of_perfectField.nonempty f.smoothLocus.2.isLocallyClosed
   123	  let x' : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ Over.mk f := Over.homMk _ ((pointEquivClosedPoint f).symm ⟨x, hxc⟩).2
   124	  let y' : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ Over.mk f := Over.homMk _ ((pointEquivClosedPoint f).symm ⟨y, hyc⟩).2
   125	  let α := (GrpObj.mulRight (A := Over.mk f) x').symm ≪≫
   126	    (GrpObj.mulRight (A := Over.mk f) y')
   127	  have hα : x' ≫ α.hom = y' := by
   128	    dsimp only [Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, α]
   129	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← Iso.eq_comp_inv]
   130	    simp [comp_lift_assoc]
   131	  have hα' : α.hom.left x = y := by
   132	    simpa [x', y', pointEquivClosedPoint] using congr(($hα).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K))
   133	  rw! [← hα', ← α.hom.left.mem_preimage, Scheme.Hom.preimage_smoothLocus_eq,
   134	    show α.hom.left ≫ f = f from α.hom.w] at hy
   135	  exact hx hy
   136	
   137	/-- **Smoothness of a group scheme from reducedness of the base change to `k̄` alone.**
   138	
   139	The criterion this project consumes in place of `smooth_of_grpObj`: for `G` a `k`-group
   140	scheme locally of finite type, `G ⟶ Spec k` is smooth as soon as the single scheme
   141	`G ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` is reduced. There is no `GeometricallyReduced` hypothesis and no
   142	quantifier over field extensions.
   143	
   144	The descent step is mathlib's, verbatim from `smooth_of_grpObj`:
   145	`MorphismProperty.of_pullback_snd_of_descendsAlong` against
   146	`@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact`, along which `@Smooth` descends
   147	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/LocalFlatDescent.lean`). The group structure transports
   148	to the base change by `Over.grpObjMkPullbackSnd`. What changes is only *where the reducedness
   149	hypothesis is taken*: `smooth_of_grpObj` derives `IsReduced` of the pullback from the
   150	`GeometricallyReduced` instance, whereas here it is supplied directly.
   151	
   152	Same strength, different attack surface — **not** a weaker hypothesis. In mathlib alone the
   153	converse (`IsReduced` over `k̄` ⟹ `GeometricallyReduced`) is unavailable, but this project owns
   154	it through `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, so at these binders the two are interprovable. See
   155	the module docstring for the correction and for why the restatement is still worth having. -/
   156	theorem smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange
   157	    (h : IsReduced (Limits.pullback f
   158	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))) :
   159	    Smooth f := by
   160	  let Ω : Type u := AlgebraicClosure K
   161	  let g : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of K) := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom <| algebraMap K Ω)
   162	  apply MorphismProperty.of_pullback_snd_of_descendsAlong
   163	    (Q := @Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact) (g := g)
   164	  · exact ⟨⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩
   165	  · letI : GrpObj (Over.mk (Limits.pullback.snd f g)) := Over.grpObjMkPullbackSnd
   166	    haveI := h
   167	    exact smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed' _
   168	
   169	end AlgebraicGeometry
